abort.single_instance_allowed: Already configured. Only a single configuration possible.

error.api_version: This rocko speaks a control API version this integration does not support. Update rocko or the integration so they match.
error.binary_not_found: There is no file at this path.
error.invalid_binary: The file is not a rocko binary: running it with `--version` did not print a rocko version.
error.invalid_pairing_code: This is not a pairing code. A code looks like `ROCKO1-` followed by two groups of hex digits; copy it whole from `rocko pair` or rocko's log.
error.pairing_expired: rocko has no open pairing code: the code expired after 10 minutes, was used already or was replaced by a newer one. Run `rocko pair` on the rocko host again and enter the new code.
error.pairing_failed: rocko did not accept the pairing. Check rocko's log, run `rocko pair` again and enter the new code.
error.pairing_rejected: rocko refused this pairing code. Check that you entered the newest code `rocko pair` printed, without changes.
error.server_certificate: rocko's certificate was made by an older rocko and lacks the name Home Assistant checks. Run `rocko identity --reissue` on the rocko host, restart rocko, then pair with a new code.
error.server_pin_mismatch: This host is not the rocko the code came from: the certificate that answers at this host and port is not the one the code names. Check the host and port, or take a code from the rocko that listens there.
error.timeout_connect: rocko did not answer in time. Check the host and port, and that the port is reachable from Home Assistant.

remote.title: Connect to rocko on another host

data_description.host: Host name or IP address of the host where rocko runs.
data_description.port: TCP port of rocko's control listener, as `ROCKO_CONTROL_LISTEN` sets it.
data_description.pairing_code: The one-time code `rocko pair` prints on the rocko host. It is valid for 10 minutes and pairs Home Assistant once; it is not stored.

remote.description:
Connect to a rocko in another container or on another host, over its control listener with mutual TLS.

On the rocko host, start rocko with its control listener on, for example `ROCKO_CONTROL_LISTEN=[::]:18557`, and make that TCP port reachable from Home Assistant. Then run `rocko pair` there (a rocko that has no client yet also logs a code at startup) and enter the code below within 10 minutes.

data_description.binary: Path of the rocko executable. Home Assistant starts it, restarts it when it fails and stops it on shutdown.

user.description: rocko is a media daemon that serves your cameras to the browser over WebRTC. Choose how Home Assistant reaches it.

sandbox_degraded.title: rocko runs with a weakened sandbox
sandbox_degraded.description:
rocko reads camera streams from the network, so each of its processes is hardened in layers. The running rocko lacks these layers: {layers}.

Start rocko as root so it can drop its privileges itself, on a kernel with seccomp and Landlock enabled. Home Assistant checks again on every connection to rocko and removes this message once the layers are in place.

sandbox_off.title: rocko runs without its sandbox
sandbox_off.description:
rocko was started with its sandbox off, so its processes run without the hardening that limits what a compromised camera stream could do.

Start rocko with its sandbox on, the default: without `--sandbox off` or `ROCKO_SANDBOX=off`. Home Assistant checks again on every connection to rocko and removes this message once the sandbox is on.
